Simulate blinded clinical trial data on an adverse event

Source: R/sim_blinded.R
sim_blinded.Rd

Generates subject-level data of a randomized two-group trial at one or more analysis times, as used in the simulations of Duncan (2026).

Usage

sim_blinded(
  n,
  k = 1,
  accrual,
  follow_up,
  analysis_time = accrual + follow_up,
  dist = c("exponential", "loglogistic"),
  par_p,
  par_d,
  dropout = 0
)

Arguments

n

Total number of subjects.

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to placebo (k:1).

accrual

Length of the accrual period (0 if all subjects enter at time 0).

follow_up

Planned follow-up time of each subject.

analysis_time

Calendar times (from the start of accrual) of the blinded analyses. The default is the time at which all subjects have completed follow-up.

dist

Distribution of the time to the event: "exponential" or "loglogistic".

par_p, par_d

Parameters of the distribution for placebo and study drug: the hazard rate for "exponential", or c(mu, sigma) for "loglogistic".

dropout

Hazard rate of dropout (0 for no dropout).

Value

A data frame with one row per subject and analysis, and the columns look (index of the analysis), analysis_time, id, group ("placebo" or "drug"; not used by the blinded analyses), entry, follow_up, event (1 if the event occurred during follow-up), event_time (time from entry to the event, NA without the event) and time_at_risk (event_time for subjects with the event, follow_up otherwise).

Details

Subjects enter the trial uniformly over [0, accrual], and round(n * k / (k + 1)) of them, chosen at random, are assigned to the study drug. The time to the first occurrence of the event follows the exponential distribution (dist = "exponential"; par_p and par_d are the hazard rates) or the log-logistic distribution of ll_cdf (dist = "loglogistic"; par_p and par_d are c(mu, sigma)). When dropout > 0, the time to dropout follows the exponential distribution with rate dropout.

At the analysis time \(\tau\), the follow-up time of a subject who entered at time \(e\) is the smallest of follow_up, \(\tau - e\) and the time to dropout, and the subject has the event if the time to the event is not larger than the follow-up time. Subjects who have not entered by \(\tau\) are not included. The same subjects and event times are used at all analysis times.

References

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 36(2), 227–244. doi:10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532

See also

sim_oc, ll_mu

Examples

set.seed(1)
# 52-week incidence of 10% (placebo) and 20% (study drug)
d <- sim_blinded(n = 200, k = 1, accrual = 26, follow_up = 52,
                 analysis_time = c(39, 78), dist = "exponential",
                 par_p = -log(0.9) / 52, par_d = -log(0.8) / 52)
table(d$look, d$event)
#>    
#>       0   1
#>   1 183  17
#>   2 169  31
